ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Real Decreto-ley 11/2018, de 31 de agosto, and Real Decreto-ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril (transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, approving the implementing Regulation of Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto-ley 7/2021 creates the Registro de Titularidades Reales, operated by the Colegio de Registradores de España, as the central beneficial-ownership register; EU Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 of 31 May 2024 (single AML/CFT rulebook) applies as of 10 July 2027. incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Companies Act (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010), including Articles 4 (minimum share capital), 20 (public deed and registration), 22–23 (deed and articles of association), 31–32 (filing and registration), and 214 (appointment of directors). Law 18/2022 amended the minimum capital rules for limited liability companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for company-name clearance; the competent provincial Registro Mercantil for incorporation registration, determined by the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), filed for registration in the provincial Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum share capital of an SL is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid on incorporation. A separate bank escrow or deposit is not generally mandatory; the deed must state the contributions and the notary must verify payment as legally required. Until share capital and the statutory reserve together reach EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to the reserve, and shareholders may be jointly liable for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital on liquidation. Registry, notarial, and name-clearance charges may apply in euros; there is no single fixed state filing fee denominated in USD.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscriptions and contributions set out in the incorporation deed and confirm that the subscribed shares are fully paid. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full address], subject to filing any required notice or amendment. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed [sole director/joint directors/board member] and [name] be appointed managing director, with the powers set out in the articles and appointment instrument. RESOLVED, that the appointed officers are authorized to obtain the Company’s tax identification number, complete tax and social-security registrations, open operating bank accounts, and make all required commercial-registry and administrative filings. The secretary is directed to record these resolutions in the Company’s minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, company-name certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit name choices in order of preference through the Central Commercial Registry’s name-certification service. Obtain a negative name certificate and provide it to the notary for the incorporation deed. Observe the certificate’s validity and renewal periods.
required_dossiers: Ordered list of proposed company names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is unavailable or rejected, submit alternative names and obtain a replacement certificate before execution of the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain tax identification and prepare incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a provisional NIF for the company using the applicable AEAT procedure, generally Form 036, and arrange execution of the public deed before a Spanish notary. Foreign documents must be apostilled or legalized where applicable and accompanied by a sworn Spanish translation. Foreign investors and directors must obtain the required Spanish tax identification numbers.
required_dossiers: Founder and director identity documents and Spanish tax identification numbers
Evidence or declaration of share-capital contributions
Powers of attorney, apostilles or legalizations, and sworn translations where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct identity, translation, legalization, capital-contribution, or articles defects identified by the notary or AEAT; re-submit the corrected Form 036 or documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders or duly authorized representatives execute the escritura pública de constitución. The deed must include the company’s identity, purpose, registered office, capital, contributions, share allocation, articles, and initial management arrangements. The notary verifies the required formalities and issues an authorized copy for filing.
required_dossiers: Evidence or required declaration of capital contributions
Powers of attorney and foreign-document formalities, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Execute a corrective or supplementary public deed if the notary identifies omissions or inconsistencies; obtain any missing legalization or identification evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the SL and complete tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil for the registered office; Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authorized deed electronically through the notary or directly as permitted, together with required tax documentation, to the competent provincial Commercial Registry. Complete the applicable regional filing for the exempt transfer tax and stamp duty transaction, obtain the definitive NIF, and update AEAT registration information. Registration is required for full corporate legal effect.
required_dossiers: Tax forms and proof of applicable filing or exemption
Evidence of payment of applicable registry and notarial charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the registrar’s qualification notice by correcting the deed or filing, supplying missing evidence, or appealing the qualification through the statutory registry-review process. Monitor any deadline stated in the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration corporate and employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT; Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social; provincial Registro Mercantil; applicable regional and municipal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the definitive NIF, file applicable tax registrations, legalize corporate books through the Commercial Registry’s electronic system within statutory time limits, and register as an employer before hiring staff. File beneficial-ownership information through the legally applicable channel and obtain any local activity, works, or site-use approvals before construction or operation.
required_dossiers: Registered incorporation deed and registry details
Tax and Social Security registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Complete omitted filings, correct registry or tax data, and regularize employer registration before commencing employment; seek the relevant authority’s written guidance where regional or municipal requirements depend on the site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent industrial authority of the Autonomous Community where the facility is located; industrial establishment registration is generally handled under Royal Decree 559/2010 through the regional industrial registry and, where applicable, the Registro Integrado Industrial.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial establishment registration (inscripción en el registro industrial) and the applicable regional prior communication or operating authorization. The precise instrument depends on the facility, process, location, and regional rules; there is no single nationwide battery-cell manufacturing operating licence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community; the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge acts where state jurisdiction applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific screening under Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment, including its Annexes I and II. Full EIA, simplified EIA, or no EIA may apply depending on the project characteristics, location, capacity, and potential effects. A facility may separately require integrated environmental authorization if it falls within the applicable categories under Royal Legislative Decree 1/2016.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: There is no single national numeric discharge or VOC limit specific to sodium-ion cell manufacture. Obtain the applicable water discharge authorization and comply with its site-specific limits, the Water Act and implementing rules, and any municipal sewer conditions. Air-emission limits and monitoring are set by the applicable authorization and air-quality rules. For solvent emissions, assess applicability and thresholds under Royal Decree 117/2003. Manage hazardous and non-hazardous production waste under Law 7/2022, including waste classification, authorized handling, traceability, and applicable producer obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before construction and operation, obtain applicable municipal planning, construction, and activity approvals and satisfy regional industrial fire-safety requirements, including Royal Decree 164/2025 where applicable. Provide the required fire-safety design and inspections, structural and equipment-load verification, and emergency planning. Complete occupational risk assessment, prevention planning, worker training, and workplace compliance under Law 31/1995 and its implementing regulations. Site-specific approval requirements depend on the Autonomous Community, municipality, building use, and process hazards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; Customs and Excise Department of AEAT (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales) for EORI and export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional corporate NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) at notarization and must file Form 036 (declaración censal de alta) with AEAT to secure the definitive NIF; the same Form 036 activates VAT registration under the ordinary regime, corporate income tax status, withholding obligations and statistical duties. Non-resident foreign entities operating in Spain without a permanent establishment must apply for a NIF-N (non-resident) or NIF-IE (EU/EEA indirect identification) via Form 036 through a legal representative, and must appoint a fiscal representative when established in a non-cooperative jurisdiction or where Spanish-source income thresholds are exceeded. Foreign suppliers engaged in exports from Spain must additionally hold an EORI number with the ES prefix issued by AEAT before filing customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box regime exists in Spain. Limited statutory elections include: (i) Spanish tax-transparency election (transparencia fiscal, art. 6 Ley 27/2014 LIS) for holding-type entities owned at least 75% by resident individuals; (ii) VAT group regime (Régimen Especial del Grupo de Entidades, art. 155 Ley 37/1992 IVA), subject to prior AEAT authorization and anti-abuse checks; (iii) election by a non-resident without a permanent establishment to be taxed under IRNR or, where a PE exists, to file under the Impuesto sobre Sociedades; (iv) election for monthly VAT refund registration (REDEME/SII enrollment); (v) option to apply the deferred-payment customs regime for import VAT. Hybrid-mismatch consequences under art. 15 quinquies LIS (ATAD 2) apply mandatorily without elective opt-out.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de-minimis registration threshold: any habitual economic activity by a resident SL manufacturer triggers mandatory registration before the first taxable transaction. Non-established EU suppliers of distance sales of goods to Spanish end recipients benefit from a €10,000 annual threshold before compulsory registration; low-value imported consignments up to €150 may be declared through the Import One Stop Shop (IOSS). A resident SL manufacturing sodium-ion battery cells will be registered from inception regardless of turnover and may claim input VAT refunds under the general, monthly (REDEME) or export-refund regimes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish Value Added Tax), governed by Ley 37/1992 and RD 1624/1992; separate quasi-VAT systems (IGIC in the Canary Islands, IPSI in Ceuta and Melilla) apply outside mainland IVA territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general threshold. Any supply of goods or services in Spanish IVA territory by an established or non-established trader requires IVA registration (Form 036/037) when the activity is habitual. The €10,000 threshold applies to intra-EU distance sales of goods only; for imports of low-value goods, the IOSS applies up to €150 per consignment. A resident manufacturing SL must be registered from the first transaction and cannot benefit from a turnover-based exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates interoperable B2B electronic invoicing under Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) and RD 1007/2023. E-invoices must be transmitted in structured interoperable formats (Facturae XAdES or equivalent) giving the buyer full access. Large enterprises (turnover > €8M) had to comply within 12 months of the regulation; all other taxable persons within 24 months. The Verifactu production regulation requires certified invoicing software to generate immutable records, apply integrity hash/QR codes, and make data accessible to AEAT upon request; no real-time pre-clearance or digital stamping is required for ordinary invoices. Taxpayers subject to the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información: turnover > €6M, VAT groups, and REDEME members) must submit every issued and received invoice record to AEAT within 8 calendar days (4 calendar days for intra-EU transactions) using the AEAT web services/API; late or partial submission triggers penalties under art. 201 LGT starting at €150 per data batch.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the EU customs territory are exempt with the right to deduct input VAT (true zero rating) under art. 21 Ley 37/1992 where (i) the goods are physically dispatched from Spanish mainland territory or from a customs warehouse in Spain by the supplier or a third party, and (ii) the goods leave the EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch. Intra-EU B2B supplies are zero rated under art. 22 LIVA when the acquirer's VIES VAT number is valid and the corresponding recapitulative statement is filed. Services to non-EU recipients (e.g., battery technology licensing, engineering consultancy, micro-mobility vehicle software) are generally outside Spanish VAT where the place-of-supply rule for B2B services points to the recipient's business establishment outside Spain. The exporting SL must hold a valid EORI number, maintain a separate export accounting ledger, and retain transport and payment evidence for at least 4 years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) bearing the EU exit-confirmation reference evidencing that the goods actually left the customs territory of the Union
Bill of Lading (or CMR consignment note or Air Waybill) signed by the carrier showing dispatch from Spain and arrival at the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT MT103 or Certificado de Remesa) evidencing collection of payment from the non-resident buyer and repatriation of the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT rigorously audits export zero-rating under art. 21 LIVA. Failure to prove the effective exit of goods, or exit after the 90-day statutory period, triggers IVA regularization at 21% plus late-payment interest (interés de demora) and a penalty of 50% of the tax evaded under art. 191 LGT, aggravated up to 100% where falsity or intent is established. Issuing zero-rated invoices without valid export documentation is sanctioned under art. 201 LGT with fines from €150 to €600,000; customs infringements additionally expose the exporter to forfeiture of goods and fines equal to the customs value under Ley 12/2021. Retrospective clawbacks extend to the four-year limitation period (indefinite in fraud cases), and where the annual defrauded amount exceeds €120,000, AEAT refers the matter to the criminal jurisdiction under art. 305 Código Penal, carrying imprisonment of 1 to 5 years plus disqualification from public subsidies and state aid. The specialised Anti-Fraud Units (ONIF and ONAUD) actively pursue carousel, round-tripping and fictitious-export schemes in the battery and e-mobility sectors.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.refund_substantiation_and_tax_repatriati: Export VAT refunds are implemented as deduction of input VAT in the periodic return (modelo 303/modelo 390) rather than as a monetary refund; exporters applying for refunds outside the ordinary returns use model 308 (form for non-established operators) or SII/REDEME accelerated monthly refunds, subject to bank-badge verification and the €6M turnover threshold for monthly direct refunds. Proceeds received after 180 days without documented extension may lead to intra-group financing transfer-pricing recharacterization under art. 16 LIS and to the recognition of late-payment interest income; repatriation documentation must be submitted with the annual corporate income tax return (modelo 200).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, operating within the Eurosystem under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank. Foreign-exchange and capital-movement matters are also governed by the European Union free-movement-of-capital framework, Spanish foreign-investment rules, Spanish anti-money-laundering legislation, and applicable reporting regulations administered by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro, which is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no general exchange-control approval requirement for foreign ownership, equity funding, dividends, interest, royalties, trade payments, or liquidation proceeds. Profit remittances are ordinarily unrestricted after corporate-tax payment, approval of annual accounts and distributable profits, satisfaction of statutory reserve requirements, and settlement of withholding-tax obligations. Payments to non-residents may require Spanish withholding-tax analysis, beneficial-owner evidence, treaty documentation, EU exemption documentation, transfer-pricing support, and anti-abuse review. Foreign direct investment from non-EU or non-EFTA investors may be subject to Spanish ex ante screening in protected sectors or where statutory thresholds and national-security or public-order conditions are met. Battery-cell manufacturing may require transaction-specific screening because of strategic-industry, critical-technology, energy-storage, or national-security considerations. Banks may require source-of-funds, ultimate-beneficial-owner, commercial-purpose, sanctions, and ownership-chain evidence before processing transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a Spanish bank, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline for converting export receipts into euros. Exporters may retain foreign-currency proceeds in domestic or foreign accounts, subject to bank documentation, tax, customs, accounting, sanctions, and statistical-reporting obligations. Export invoices and customs declarations must support the underlying transaction, and banks may request transport documents, commercial invoices, purchase orders, bills of lading, customs data, and proof of delivery. Cross-border balances, transactions, or payment flows may trigger Banco de España external-sector reporting, including Formulario ETE where applicable and according to the relevant reporting thresholds and periodicity. Contractual requirements under financing arrangements, export-credit insurance, grants, or customer contracts may impose separate repatriation or account-use obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for an EU or EEA-authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution that is passported into Spain and can provide SEPA and international payment services. Low for an offshore digital EMI without EU authorisation, passporting, or a regulated Spanish or EEA partner. An EMI account is not a bank deposit, does not itself provide deposit-guarantee protection, and may not provide credit, unrestricted cash-management, trade-finance, or foreign-exchange services outside its authorisation. Safeguarding, transaction limits, correspondent-bank dependencies, sanctions screening, account-freeze risk, and weaker acceptance by customs, auditors, lenders, and large industrial counterparties must be assessed. A regulated Spanish bank should remain the primary account for share capital, payroll, tax, customs, letters of credit, and critical supplier payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available through qualified electronic identification, video identification, powers of attorney, and verified corporate documentation, subject to each bank's policy. Banks commonly require in-person attendance or enhanced verification for non-resident directors, complex ownership chains, high-risk jurisdictions, cash-intensive activity, strategic manufacturing, large initial transfers, foreign politically exposed persons, or inconsistent business profiles. The company should maintain a Spanish registered office, Spanish tax identification number, beneficial-owner records, evidence of operating premises, and a locally authorised signatory. A notarised or bank-accepted power of attorney, apostille or legalisation, sworn translation where required, and current registry certificates may be necessary for representatives acting without the directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, opaque holding companies, nominee shareholders, trusts, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate chart to natural-person ownership, certificates of incorporation and good standing, shareholder register, passports and residential evidence for all relevant individuals, beneficial-owner declaration, board resolutions, powers of attorney, and a written explanation of ownership rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital transfer inconsistent with the stated share capital, business plan, or historical financial profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement, board and shareholder resolutions, bank statements showing the source account, audited or management accounts of the funding entity, tax returns or financial statements, source-of-wealth memorandum, investment committee approval, and payment reference identifying the legal purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Battery-cell manufacturing classified as strategic, dual-use, environmentally sensitive, or enhanced-risk activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, product and technical description, end-use and end-user policy, sanctions and export-control policy, supplier and customer screening procedure, environmental and industrial permits or applications, waste and chemical-management controls, transport and dangerous-goods procedures, and evidence that no military or prohibited end use is intended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving jurisdictions, counterparties, banks, vessels, or persons subject to sanctions or heightened country risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening results, counterparty ownership records, end-user certificates, commercial contracts, invoices, customs and transport documents, origin and destination evidence, legal review of EU, UN, UK, and US exposure where relevant, and documented escalation and approval controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-value export receipts, rapid movement of funds, pass-through activity, or use of personal, virtual-asset, or unrelated third-party accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling 12-month cash-flow forecast, customer and supplier master file, payment-approval matrix, segregation-of-duties policy, reconciliation controls, expected transaction-volume schedule, treasury policy, explanation of payment intermediaries, and prohibition of third-party settlement absent documented commercial justification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-direct-investment screening, ownership change, or capital increase involving a non-EU or non-EFTA investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investor identity and ownership information, transaction structure, valuation, sector analysis, national-security and public-order assessment, filing or exemption analysis under Spanish foreign-investment rules, evidence of any required declaration or authorisation, and legal confirmation of closing conditions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete Spanish corporate records, unverified registered office, inactive tax status, or mismatch between registry, tax, beneficial-owner, and bank information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Registro Mercantil certificate, deed of incorporation and amendments, Spanish tax-identification certificate, proof of registered office and operating premises, current director and signatory records, beneficial-ownership filing or declaration, licences, and reconciled corporate-information checklist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for cash deposits, unexplained trade-finance structures, unusual letters of credit, over-invoicing, under-invoicing, or circular transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying purchase and sales contracts, independent pricing support, customs classification, Incoterms, shipping documents, inspection certificates, insurance, customer credit assessment, letter-of-credit text, transaction approval record, and documented three-way reconciliation among goods, invoice, and payment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route investment through the Spanish company's account at a regulated Spanish or EEA bank using SEPA for euro transfers or SWIFT for non-euro and non-EEA transfers. The payment reference should identify the precise legal basis, such as share-capital subscription, capital increase, share premium, shareholder loan, or documented equity contribution. Before receipt, provide the bank with the executed subscription or loan agreement, corporate approvals, investor ownership chart, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, and expected-use schedule. Following receipt, issue the bank certificate required for the notarial incorporation or capital-increase process where applicable, record the transaction in the accounting ledger, complete Registro Mercantil filings, and assess Spanish foreign-investment declarations or screening. Do not route capital through a personal account, unrelated affiliate, unregulated payment provider, or anonymous third party. For non-euro funding, document the exchange rate, conversion date, hedge treatment, transfer fees, and accounting value. Retain SWIFT confirmations, bank statements, agreements, board resolutions, tax records, and reconciliation evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly represented by MT103 or its ISO 20022 successor equivalent, for international payments. Use commercial letters of credit, preferably irrevocable and subject to UCP 600, for higher-risk suppliers, new counterparties, strategic equipment, or jurisdictional risk. Documentary collections may be used where the risk profile permits. Every payment should match an approved purchase order or contract, invoice, beneficiary account, customs classification, Incoterms, transport documents, sanctions screening, and goods-receipt or shipment evidence. For imports, maintain customs declarations, proof of origin, tariff data, VAT evidence, and dangerous-goods or battery transport documentation where relevant. For exports, reconcile customer receipts to invoices and customs records. Banks may require purpose information, beneficiary declarations, end-use evidence, and enhanced review for battery technology, lithium or sodium compounds, energy-storage equipment, dual-use items, or strategic counterparties. Avoid split payments, unexplained third-party settlement, and payments to accounts in jurisdictions unrelated to the transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorised bank for forecast or committed receivables and payables, supported by documented hedging purpose, notional limits, maturity matching, and counterparty confirmation.

Non-deliverable forwards where offered by an authorised bank and legally suitable for the relevant currency, with cash settlement, documented exposure, EMIR classification and reporting analysis, collateral terms, and counterparty-risk limits.
Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for recurring funding or long-term currency mismatches, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, valuation, collateral, accounting, and EMIR requirements.
FX spot transactions and rolling hedges for operational currency conversion, supported by treasury approvals and segregation of duties.
Currency options or collars for asymmetric exposure protection, subject to suitability, premium, valuation, accounting, and board-approved risk limits.

The company should execute derivatives only with authorised EU or otherwise lawfully accessible counterparties, maintain a written hedging policy, document the underlying exposure, monitor mark-to-market and collateral, assess clearing and trade-reporting obligations under EMIR, and avoid speculative or unapproved leveraged positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Memoria Anual - Filing of Annual Accounts and Management Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: One month after the general meeting of shareholders approves the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines between 300 and 3,000 EUR for late filing; administrative strike-off possible after three months of delinquency

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SL exceeds two of the following: turnover exceeding 2 million EUR, total assets exceeding 1 million EUR, or average headcount exceeding 50 employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC) for non-listed entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual confirmation required; beneficial ownership details must be notified to the Registro Mercantil within one month of any change

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 150-450 USD per year for virtual registered office or agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,000-5,000 USD for certified audit if mandated or elected

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created SL entities for the first two tax periods with positive taxable base, subject to job and activity restrictions; unlimited tax loss carryforward, subject to offset limitations; 25% R&D tax credit on qualifying expenditure; partial exemption under the ETVE (holding) regime; no general statutory tax holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed through the Spanish Tax Agency's electronic portal (Sede Electrónica de la AEAT); mandatory e-filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (provisional quarterly settlements via Modelo 202/205/206 apply to certain taxpayers).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days of the sixth month after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year entity, the filing window is 1 July through 25 July.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification file: NIF (Spanish tax identification number), company name, tax address, fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the permanent establishment's Spanish NIF and the parent company's foreign tax identification details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base (Base Imponible) after statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only the taxable base attributable to the Spanish permanent establishment under the double tax agreement.
Use 25% unless a special reduced rate is available under the applicable law; treaty-protected permanent establishment rates do not bypass this statutory rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, credits, and reliefs applied to the tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only credits directly related to Spanish-source income or permanent establishment activity may be claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable or refundable amount after withholdings and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle the net liability via bank transfer or initiate a refund claim using the AEAT refund procedure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers General Tax Law (LGT) art. 27 surcharges of 5%, 10%, 15%, or 20% of the unpaid tax depending on the delay, plus default interest; failure to file within 12 months triggers a fixed penalty plus 20% surcharge; incorrect or incomplete filings may be sanctioned under LGT art. 198 with penalties up to EUR 3,000 or 5% of omitted amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (non-resident income tax general rate); 0% typically applicable to qualifying EU parent companies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; reduced rates from 5% to 10% under most tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must furnish an original tax residency certificate (often Form ESD/TRC) from the foreign tax authority. The Spanish paying entity may apply the reduced withholding at source if the certificate is valid; otherwise the non-resident must file Form 210 (Refund of Excess Withholding) with the AEAT within the four-year statutory time limit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 19% statutory withholding on non-residents receiving royalties and interest; reduced to 0% for qualifying associated companies under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive; applicable DTA rates generally range from 0% to 10% for interest and 10% for royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory full Local File and Master File required where consolidated group net turnover equals or exceeds EUR 45 million; for smaller taxpayers, simplified documentation applies unless related-party transactions exceed EUR 100,000 per transaction type (goods) or EUR 25,000 (services).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies an anti-abuse economic substance doctrine through CIT art. 15 LIS, controlled foreign corporation rules (art. 100 LIS), and the general anti-avoidance clause (art. 159 LIS). Non-resident treaty relief and special favourable regimes such as the ETVE holding regime require real management, qualified personnel, and physical premises in Spain, with shell or letterbox entities automatically rebutted as lacking sufficient economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting taxable income through false invoices, undisclosed bank accounts, or accounting manipulation, where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code art. 305: imprisonment from 1 to 6 years, a fine of up to six times the amount evaded, loss of tax benefits, and mandatory restitution of the evaded amount plus default interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ordered or knowingly accepted the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax. They may face travel bans, provisional detention, disqualification from managing commercial entities, and seizure of corporate and personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SL as an empty conduit with no employees, premises, or genuine management functions to divert profits, claim treaty benefits, or facilitate undisclosed asset holding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR re-characterisation, denial of treaty and directive benefits, 25% surcharge on artificial transactions; administrative fines under Spanish LGT and AML Act 10/2010; dissolution proceedings in egregious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the corporate tax debt under LGT art. 42.2 if their recklessness caused insolvency; severe cases trigger civil liability, asset tracing, travel restrictions, and disqualification orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering and False Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Undocumented cross-border payments, circular Swift wiring, overstated purchases through false invoices to move funds outside official books, or ignoring beneficial ownership due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML Act 10/2010: fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 for serious infringements; tax penalties under LGT art. 191 of 50% to 150% of the evaded base; freezing of bank accounts and forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face imprisonment up to six years under Criminal Code art. 301 for money laundering, travel bans, personal asset seizures, and civil liability for damages arising from the laundering operation.
